memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Altogether, Enoch lived a total of 365 years. Enoch walked faithfully with God; then he was no more, because God took him away. - Gen 5:23-24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the drumbeat of the chapter falls silent. For everyone else the record ends, "and then he died." But not for Enoch. Of him it says, "he was no more, because God took him away." Enoch did not die - God simply took him home. His walk with God on earth flowed seamlessly into being with God forever.

What a picture of where a life of walking with God leads. Enoch's daily fellowship with the Lord did not end at a grave; it deepened into eternal fellowship in God's presence. The One he walked with for 365 years welcomed him home.

The New Testament confirms it: "By faith Enoch was taken from this life, so that he did not experience death... for before he was taken, he was commended as one who pleased God" (Heb 11:5). His secret was faith - a life that trusted and pleased God.

Enoch's story is a bright promise shining in a chapter full of death. It reminds us that for those who walk with God, death is not the end but a homecoming. Jesus made this certain: "whoever lives by believing in me will never die" (John 11:26). One day, all who belong to Christ will be taken to be with Him forever (1 Thess 4:17). Walk with God now, and you will be with Him then.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does your walk with God give you hope beyond the grave?
- Are you living to please God by faith, as Enoch did?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that a life of walking with You leads home to You. Help me please You by faith, and give me hope that death is a homecoming in Christ.
